challenge_007_goal: Authentic roller Microduck completes a figure-eight around two cones and stops inside a 0.25 m parking target across three perturbed seeds, with no cone contacts or falls.
challenge_007_story: Human skating hook, early cone miss, one understandable steering/timing decision, uninterrupted figure-eight, then a precision-stop wow moment.
challenge_007_baseline: The frozen official roller policy with a 0.32 m/s, 2.2 yaw-gain waypoint layer reached 9/24 waypoints and made nearly one loop without touching a cone, but tipped during the first tight reversal on all three perturbed seeds at 3.70-4.06 s. Baseline fails 0/3.
challenge_007_baseline_diagnosis: The first bottleneck is turning stability, not obstacle clearance: cone contacts were 0/3 while all three cases fell near the same high-curvature transition. Search lower forward speed and yaw gain before changing the course.
challenge_007_search_1: A bounded 18-candidate grid over 0.26-0.38 m/s forward speed, 1.8-3.0 yaw gain, and 0.10-0.14 m waypoint capture radius produced no passing controller. Every candidate failed before completing both loops; the selected rank-best setting still fell on all three seeds after reaching only 3-8 of 24 waypoints. This rejects constant-speed point-to-point steering for the course.
challenge_007_search_1_best: 0.32 m/s forward speed, 1.8 yaw gain, 0.10 m waypoint capture radius; 0/3 seeds passed, zero cone contacts, all three fell at 2.88-4.02 s.
challenge_007_final_attempt: A final distinct 12-candidate pure-pursuit search added lookahead, curvature-aware slowing, and the official roller policy's lateral command channel. It improved one seed to 78.21% route progress and avoided a fall for the full 18 seconds on another, but no seed completed either loop; the rank-best setting also accumulated cone contacts. Challenge closed as a measured failure after three bounded runs.
challenge_007_status: published_failure_story: the frozen roller policy could not execute the required tight figure-eight reliably through its public velocity interface; the Short clearly reports 0/3 passes
challenge_008_goal: Lift one Microduck foot and hold a genuine single-support balance for at least 2.0 seconds across three perturbed starts without the raised foot touching down or the torso falling.
challenge_008_baseline: The frozen official stand policy held ordinary two-foot stance for the full 3.0-second measurement on all three perturbed seeds: both-foot contact ratios, double-support ratio, and minimum upright score were all 1.0. Mean foot separation was 0.079196 m and maximum absolute COM offset from the foot midpoint was 0.000316 m. This is a calibration baseline, not a one-leg success claim.
challenge_008_attempt_1: A 64-candidate exhaustive search combined four lateral support shifts with every sign combination of right hip-roll, hip-pitch, knee, and ankle residuals at the declared 0.20-rad cap. No candidate passed any seed. The rank-best pose cleared the right foot only 0.02-0.04 seconds versus the 2.0-second gate and reduced left-foot contact to 0.887-0.893, while the torso remained upright at 0.9984 or better. This simultaneous shift-and-lift method is rejected.
challenge_008_attempt_2: A distinct 30-candidate staged search first shifted support for 1.5 seconds with bounded hip-roll residuals and the authentic head-roll command, then lifted either leg. The best mirrored case used the head as a counterweight, raised the left foot, and reproducibly extended valid single support from attempt 1's 0.02-0.04 seconds to 0.12 seconds on all three seeds. It still failed the 2.0-second gate and support-foot contact over the full evaluation was only 0.827-0.853, so no success is claimed.
challenge_008_final_attempt: The final 192-candidate search varied authentic head-roll counterweight targets, four lead times, and every sign combination of the raised left leg at the 0.20-rad residual cap. Zero candidates passed. The best pose reproducibly held valid single support for 0.16 seconds on all three seeds versus the 2.0-second gate, with support-foot contact ratios of 0.793-0.800. Challenge closed as a measured failure after three distinct attempts.
challenge_008_status: published_failure_story: the bounded frozen-policy interface improved a left-foot lift to 0.16 seconds but could not sustain genuine one-leg balance; the Short clearly reports the missed 2.0-second gate
challenge_010_goal: Bittle X self-rights within 5 seconds from left, right, and back tip-over starts, then walks 1.0 meter within 10 seconds without a second fall using a command interface that can map to its ESP32 BiBoard.
challenge_010_story: Pet-dog stumble hook, robot tip-over, one recovery decision, self-righting wow moment, one-meter walk, and an honest sim-to-real caveat.
challenge_010_provenance: The audited MuJoCo model is the third-party Apache-2.0 MarcHesse/bittle-mujoco project pinned at cbadd735ff1ee11113a681bb20eeb2fc013aa29c. It reuses MIT-licensed official Petoi meshes and OpenCatESP32 gait data, but it is not an official Petoi simulator. Official OpenCatESP32 firmware is pinned at 84dd6eff307eb2f4af6f9cbdf72f04e7d71beecf and exposes the rc recovery and wkF walk skills through the k skill-command interface.
challenge_010_source_lock: Pinned simulator and firmware inputs were fetched reproducibly; official rc (107 integers) and wkF (932 integers) payloads were extracted byte-for-value unchanged and hashed before baseline work.
challenge_010_skill_decode: The official rc payload decodes to five 20-byte behavior frames with 16 joint targets, speed, delay, and trigger fields; its nominal firmware-style sequence is about 3.096 seconds before physical servo timing. The official wkF payload decodes to 116 eight-leg gait frames. Both raw and mirrored recovery target sets are ready for baseline replay.
challenge_010_stock_recovery_baseline: The unchanged official rc leg targets recovered the third-party MuJoCo Bittle from declared left, right, and dorsal-back starts. Raw and mirrored variants both passed the 5-second gate; each first held upright score >=0.8 and torso height >=0.045 m for 0.25 s at 3.068 s. This is a simulation baseline, not real-hardware evidence.
challenge_010_stock_recovery_walk: The unchanged official rc→wkF sequence recovered from all three declared starts and completed 10 seconds without a second fall, but failed the 1 m distance gate. Maximum forward progress was 0.2538 m from left, 0.2868 m from right, and 0.1872 m from dorsal-back. Baseline fails 0/3 on distance, not stability.
challenge_010_walk_diagnosis: Stock wkF keeps making stable forward progress, but only at 0.01830-0.02823 m/s after recovery versus the 0.10 m/s gate. It would need about 35.4-54.6 seconds to cover 1 m. The bounded next product decision is official trF after the same unchanged rc recovery, not more recovery tuning.
challenge_010_official_trot_attempt: Switching from official wkF to unchanged official trF improved 10-second progress to 0.7676 m from left and 0.7857 m from right, but dorsal-back reached only 0.2639 m. All three stayed upright with no second fall, yet none reached 1 m. Stock-skill engineering is closed as 0/3 full passes; produce an honest recovery-success/speed-limit story rather than tuning official tables repeatedly.

challenge_012_architecture_v2: Use the shipped frozen walk policy for a disclosed deck-relative recenter command, combined with a learned stance residual; train only on harbor and chop
challenge_012_training_attempt_2: Always-on frozen walk-policy recentering passed 20 seconds on all harbor seeds with 0.211-0.240 m drift, but reduced chop survival to 5.68-5.86 seconds; held-out surge was not touched

challenge_012_training_attempt_4: The in-memory candidate appeared to pass all harbor gates with 6.98-7.72 second chop survival, but re-evaluation of the published seven-decimal parameters passed only one harbor gate and yielded 6.72-8.02 second chop survival
challenge_012_training_attempt_5: Chop-focused continuation did not improve the reproducible candidate: serialized parameters pass all three harbor gates but chop fails at 5.56-6.20 seconds; held-out surge was not touched
challenge_012_reproducibility_audit: Re-evaluation showed chaotic fall timing is sensitive to seven-decimal gain rounding; candidate metrics must be computed after twelve-decimal serialization before future claims
challenge_012_training_attempt_6: Twelve-decimal post-serialization evaluation passes all three harbor gates and improves chop survival to 6.18-8.04 seconds, but chop still fails; held-out surge was not touched
challenge_012_attempt_6_diagnosis: All three chop runs exit the deck bounds without direct foot-floor contact: seeds 29 and 83 cross the lateral edge at 8.04 and 7.90 seconds, while seed 197 falls behind longitudinally at 6.18 seconds
challenge_012_training_attempt_7: Eight-gain axis-specific wave feed-forward search retained the zero-feed-forward attempt-6 controller as best; all harbor gates still pass, chop remains 6.18-8.04 seconds, and held-out surge was not touched
challenge_012_attempt_7_saturation_conta: Longitudinal walk commands saturate for 57.47-58.71% of chop steps; sustained contact loss begins at 2.86-3.02 s, before 6.18-8.04 s deck exits; lateral commands and joint residuals also saturate materially
challenge_012_training_attempt_8: A 32-candidate contact-aware command-latching search preserved all three harbor gates, but its best candidate reduced worst chop survival from 6.18 s to 5.66 s and mean chop survival by 1.4333 s; rejected
challenge_012_stance_phase_diagnosis: Longitudinal command saturation is only 8.25-16.67% during double support but 69.03-81.55% during single or zero support; the PD layer reacts after useful support is lost
challenge_012_training_attempt_9: A 24-candidate double-support-triggered anticipatory step-pulse search preserved all three harbor gates for its best candidate, but chop still failed and worst-case survival fell from 6.18 s to 5.76 s; rejected
challenge_012_attempt_10_contract: A 14-feature linear residual recovery policy explicitly observes deck-relative state, deck motion, left/right foot support, double/zero support, and phase age; bounded to 0.08 m/s longitudinal and 0.06 m/s lateral residuals above the frozen walking policy
challenge_012_training_attempt_10: A 90-candidate contact- and phase-aware linear recovery-policy search preserved all three harbor gates and improved worst chop survival from 6.18 s to 6.86 s; mean chop survival changed from 7.3733 s to 7.3467 s and full chop gates remain 0/3, so the policy is accepted only as a refinement starting point
challenge_012_attempt_10_verification: Independent re-evaluation exactly reproduced the serialized policy's 3/3 harbor passes, 0/3 chop passes, 6.86 s worst chop survival, and 7.3467 s mean chop survival
challenge_012_training_attempt_11: A 120-candidate local refinement preserved all three harbor gates and improved the serialized recovery policy from 6.86 s worst / 7.3467 s mean chop survival to 7.10 s worst / 7.4333 s mean; full chop gates remain 0/3
challenge_012_attempt_11_ablation: Removing the learned constant bias caused the largest worst-chop loss (−2.86 s), raising fixed-wave-phase overfit risk; among state-dependent groups, removing deck-motion features caused the largest loss (−2.58 s), followed by relative state (−1.56 s) and support phase (−1.52 s)
challenge_012_attempt_11_phase_audit: Across five motion-phase offsets and three seeds per profile, attempt 11 passed 13/15 harbor gates and 0/15 chop gates; worst/mean chop survival fell to 4.10/5.5133 s. Removing the constant bias passed 14/15 harbor gates and reached 4.18/5.0520 s. Phase-shift generalization is rejected; held-out surge remained untouched.
challenge_012_training_attempt_12: A 56-candidate search trained across three harbor/chop wave phases with the constant bias forced to zero. Post-serialization training evaluation passed 9/9 harbor gates and improved worst chop survival from 4.02 s to 4.34 s, with 0/9 chop gates.
challenge_012_attempt_12_verification: Independent evaluation across five phases passed 15/15 harbor gates and improved worst chop survival from the no-recovery controller's 3.88 s to 4.34 s; mean chop survival was 5.0973 s versus 5.2453 s and full chop gates remain 0/15. Held-out surge remained untouched.
challenge_012_attempt_12_failure_diagnos: All 15 phase-audit chop runs exit the rear longitudinal edge. Forward command saturation spans 13.90-37.55%, backward saturation is 0%, sustained contact loss begins 0.76-3.50 s before exit, and the learned recovery residual never saturates. The limiting problem is delayed forward foot placement under weakening support, not lateral authority or residual bounds.
challenge_012_training_attempt_13: A 54-candidate grid search for a support- and velocity-triggered forward-command floor preserved all 9 training-phase harbor gates and improved worst/mean chop survival from 4.34/5.2956 s to 4.48/5.4467 s on the three search phases.
challenge_012_attempt_13_verification: Independent five-phase evaluation preserved 15/15 harbor gates but reduced worst chop survival from 4.34 s to 4.10 s; mean chop survival improved from 5.0973 s to 5.1867 s and full chop gates remained 0/15. The trigger is rejected as a worst-case regression; held-out surge remained untouched.
challenge_012_attempt_13_timing_diagnosi: The trigger fires 1.16-5.06 s before sustained contact loss, helps 8/15 chop runs, and hurts 7/15. Regressions cluster at phase offsets 0.0, 0.6, and 0.9. Longer lead and higher duty correlate positively with survival delta (0.4921 and 0.3876), so excessive trigger timing or duty does not support a smooth-threshold follow-up.
challenge_012_training_attempt_14: A 32-candidate search applied a bounded sagittal residual only to the unsupported swing leg, scaled by rearward position and velocity risk. It preserved 9/9 training-phase harbor gates and improved worst chop survival from 4.34 s to 4.40 s, though mean fell from 5.2956 s to 5.1511 s.
challenge_012_attempt_14_verification: Independent five-phase evaluation preserved 15/15 harbor gates and improved worst/mean chop survival from 4.34/5.0973 s to 4.40/5.1333 s. Full chop gates remain 0/15. The official walking policy stayed frozen and held-out surge remained untouched.
challenge_012_training_attempt_15: A 27-candidate local search around attempt 14's position, velocity, and swing-hip amplitude settings found no improvement across all five audited phases. On three new initial-state seeds the unchanged attempt-14 configuration passed 13/15 harbor gates because two runs narrowly missed the 0.95 deck-contact-ratio gate (0.948 and 0.947); chop remained 0/15 with 4.10 s worst / 5.2547 s mean survival. challenge_012_attempt_15_harbor_diagnosi: The two shaped-controller harbor misses are contact-quality misses, not falls or deck exits. Swing-foot shaping and no shaping each pass 13/15 gates but their miss sets do not overlap. On the shaped controller's misses, no-support duty increases by 0.010-0.017 and support transitions increase by 16-43 versus no shaping, implicating phase chatter rather than insufficient residual amplitude.
challenge_012_training_attempt_16: An 18-candidate swing-phase-local hysteresis and minimum-hold search was screened only on harbor across five phases and six seeds. The ungated controller passed 28/30 with 0.947 minimum and 0.9570 mean contact ratio; no gated candidate exceeded 28/30, and the best gated minimum fell to 0.946. challenge_012_training_attempt_18: A 12-candidate low-pass RMS deck-angle selector search kept swing-foot shaping fully off in harbor and enabled it for 55.12% of chop steps. challenge_012_attempt_18_verification: Across three unseen seeds and five unseen phase offsets, the selector stayed fully inactive in harbor and preserved 14/15 harbor gates, but rough-water worst survival regressed from 3.88 s to 3.80 s while mean rose from 4.9053 s to 4.9747 s. Rejected; held-out surge untouched.
challenge_012_attempt_18_timing_diagnosi: Across 15 unseen chop cases, selector onset spans 2.08-2.60 s and is uncorrelated with survival delta (-0.0272). This supports one bounded test of longer continuous rough-water activation while retaining zero harbor activation.
challenge_012_training_attempt_19: A final five-candidate exposure search held the 0.06 rad onset fixed and lowered the off threshold from 0.048 to 0.0 across calibration and unseen splits. Swing-foot shaping is retired; surge remained untouched.
challenge_012_walk_policy_interface_audi: The frozen walk network exposes one 61D observation input and one 14D action output at the native 50 Hz rate. Its public command contract provides vx, vy, yaw rate, and head targets only; it has no external gait-phase, cadence, or stance-duty input. Direct cadence tuning is therefore unavailable without changing the policy contract. A native-rate stand/walk arbiter is the remaining freeze-safe, non-joint-residual route to test longer support.
challenge_012_training_attempt_20: A 12-candidate native-rate support-aware stand/walk arbiter was screened across four harbor phases and three seeds. The selected 4-step support confirmation, 2-step stand hold, and 6-step walk cooldown improved harbor gates from 11/12 to 12/12, minimum contact ratio from 0.946 to 0.951, and mean contact ratio from 0.9558 to 0.9577. It used the stand policy for 2.89% of steps. No new joint residual was added; official weights stayed frozen; chop and surge were untouched.
challenge_012_attempt_20_verification: On 15 unseen cases per profile, the arbiter preserved 14/15 harbor gates but regressed minimum/mean harbor contact ratio from 0.948/0.9576 to 0.946/0.9569, so it was rejected under the no-harbor-regression rule. Rough-chop worst/mean survival improved from 3.88/4.9053 s to 3.92/5.0667 s, with 0/15 gates. Official weights stayed frozen; surge remained untouched.
challenge_012_training_attempt_21: The calibrated RMS deck-angle selector kept support arbitration exactly off across all 45 harbor cases, reproducing every baseline metric. Across 45 rough-chop cases it activated for 54.04% of steps, but verified double-support windows allowed the stand policy on only 0.29% of steps. Worst survival stayed 3.88 s and mean fell from 5.0840 s to 5.0400 s; 0/45 chop gates passed. Rejected; official weights frozen and surge untouched.
challenge_012_moving_support_policy_cont: Version 1 defines a separate 63-observation, 14-action rough-water residual policy at 50 Hz. It leaves official ONNX files byte-identical, limits joint residuals to 0.20 rad and 0.04 rad per control step, trains through static, harbor, partial-chop, and full-chop curriculum stages, requires 15/15 unseen harbor and 15/15 unseen chop gates, and keeps surge sealed until a serialized checkpoint passes both.
challenge_012_rl_stack: Pinned Gymnasium 1.3.0 and Stable-Baselines3 2.9.0 on Python 3.13.7 with Torch 2.14.0. The 63-observation/14-action MuJoCo environment passes the SB3 environment checker, deterministic reset, five-step smoke test, action-magnitude and 0.04-rad step-rate limits, and explicit surge rejection.
challenge_012_stage0_ppo_smoke: A bounded 128-step PPO run on static support passed checkpoint save/reload with identical deterministic predictions and a clean 10-step loaded-model rollout. challenge_012_stage0_static_sanity: Across five fixed seeds, the 128-step PPO checkpoint and exact zero-residual baseline each passed 5/5 static 20-second gates with 1.0 deck-contact ratio. challenge_012_stage1_harbor_probe: A 512-step PPO continuation at 0.25 harbor motion kept 5/5 harbor cases at 20 seconds with full contact and reduced maximum harbor displacement from 0.099473 m to 0.099400 m. The deficit is 49-62 repeated no-support bouts per rollout, each at most 0.04 s, rather than falls, long flight, action-rate clipping, or insufficient centering. Next target the reward for continuous post-ramp support; do not add centering authority.

The weakest case moves to seed 29 at phase 0.3 s with 0.935 contact; seed 197 at phase 1.2 s is the only case whose support chatter worsens. The remaining minimum is phase-sensitive, and a 512-step two-environment probe exposes the harbor learner to only one randomly sampled phase before the rollout ends.

challenge_012_stage3_support_timing_diag: Across all five declared harbor phases, the phase-balanced candidate reduced mean post-ramp no-support bouts from 58.2 to 49.2 and support transitions from 248.4 to 232.0 while raising mean post-ramp contact from 0.9300 to 0.9420. challenge_012_stage3_residual_drift_diag: Across the five declared harbor cases, phase-balanced training increased mean absolute residual from 0.005982 to 0.013049 rad (2.18x) while reducing maximum displacement by 0.030784 m and improving mean contact by 0.0108. In both, right hip roll was the dominant action shift; the regularized action-head L2 change was 1.079x the parent action-head norm. The inherited PPO uses learning rate 3e-4, clip 0.2, two epochs, and no target-KL stop. This localizes the failure to an oversized first policy update and justifies optimizer-level trust-region controls.
